Firms’ median expectation for U.S. inflation moved down to 3.0 percent after rising to 3.5 percent last quarter. The mean expectation was 3.4 percent, down from 4.2 percent last quarter.

One-Year-Ahead U.S. Inflation Expectations

### Long-Term Median Inflation Expectations Hold Steady [...] For the longer run, firms’ median expectations of the average annual price increase that U.S. consumers will experience over the next 10 years held steady from last quarter at 3.0 percent. The mean expectation rose to 7.3 percent from 5.9 percent, after falling last quarter.

results.content:
Inflation. Median one-year inflation expectations fell by 0.1 percentage point to 3.6%. Medium-term expectations were unchanged at 3.3%, as were longer-term expectations at 3.0%.
 Gas prices. Year-ahead gas price growth expectations rose by 1.4 percentage points to 2.9%.
 Unemployment expectations. The mean probability that unemployment will be higher a year from now rose by 1.1 percentage points to 42.8%.
